title: Old Tuxedo Band days and ceasing to play out in the 1920s
summary: He recalls playing with the Tuxedo Band, Oscar Randall and others, stopping playing out in the 1920s and now playing occasionally with the Chalice family.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, that's what I did. I got my own arrangement copyrighted, you see. And, oh, it went on nice, it went on nice. We should sing that. Yeah. And I was fixing to get the boys together, because I, very few musicians I know now, they all, you're all my old musician friends, they're all gone. I suppose. Yeah, I remember, I remember, I remember, I remember, I remember, I remember, I remember, and Peter Brokaw, and about some of the only ones that I can remember back that time, you understand? I, I, I don't know of any other of the old musicians. Of course, that was Papa Celestine, but I remember when he came here, when Papa Celestine first came here, and we played with the, uh, uh, Tuxedo Band, which he still kept that name, Tuxedo Band. And, B.B. Ripley was the first organizer of that Tuxedo Band. Well, I played with them, they all played, I played with them all, I played with them. Oscar Randall used to have a band, I used to play with him. And, uh, there's another fellow, I forget his name, the last band I played with. But, all that's over 30, 35 years ago, you know what I mean? And I stopped playing out and so forth. When did you stop about? Oh, I, I stopped playing as far back as the, uh, a lot of part of the twenties. I, I mean, playing out here. No, that's your plan. I kept my little playing here, and I grew up in the horse with my friend, uptown, uh, Mr. Chalice. He has a musical family, Chalice has a musical family, and, uh, they all play music. And, used to go up there, and, I still go up some time. Since my wife died, well, I don't get around so much, but I used to go up there and play with them, you know, and so forth. And now since authorized, I've been getting a hold of my fingers, it's kind of difficult. Yeah, so I don't, I don't have to touch the piano now anymore.
